edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 1, Paris 1844), Ad Scapulam, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Non te terremus, qui nec timemus: sed velim, ut omnes salvos facere possimus, monendo μὴ θεομαχεῖν. Potes et officio jurisdictionis tuae fungi, et humanitatis meminisse, vel quia et vos sub gladio estis. Quid enim amplius tibi mandatur, quam nocentes confessos damnare, negantes autem ad tormenta revocare? Videtis ergo quomodo ipsi vos contra mandata faciatis, ut confessos negare cogatis. Adeo confitemini innocentes esse nos, quos damnare statim ex confessione non vultis. Si autem contenditis ad elidendos nos, jam ergo innocentiam expugnatis. Quanti autem praesides, et constantiores et crudeliores, dissimulaverunt ab hujusmodi caussis! ut Cincius Severus, qui Thystri ipse dedit remedium, quomodo responderent christiani, ut dimitti possent; ut Vespronius Candidus, qui christianum quasi tumultuosum civibus suis satisfacere dimisit; ut Asper, qui modice vexatum hominem, et statim dejectum, nec sacrificium compulit facere, ante professus inter advocatos et adsessores, dolere se incidisse in hanc caussam. Pudens etiam missum ad se christianum in elogio concussione ejus intellecta dimisit, scisso eodem elogio, sine accusatore negans se auditurum hominem secundum mandatum. Haec omnia tibi et de officio suggeri possunt, et ab eisdem advocatis, qui ipsi beneficia habent Christianorum, licet acclament, quae volunt. Nam et cujusdam notarius cum a daemone praecipitaretur, liberatus est: et quorumdam propinquus et puerulus, et quanti honesti viri (de vulgaribus enim non dicimus) aut a daemoniis aut valetudinibus remediati sunt! Ipse etiam Severus pater Antonini, Christianorum memor fuit. Nam et Proculum christianum qui Torpacion cognominabatur, Euhodeae procuratorem, qui eum per oleum aliquando curaverat, requisivit, et in palatio suo habuit usque ad mortem ejus: quem et Antoninus optime noverat lacte christiano educatus. Sed et clarissimas foeminas et clarissimos viros Severus sciens hujus sectae esse, non modo non laesit, verum et testimonio exornavit, et populo furenti in nos palam restitit. Marcus quoque Aurelius in Germanica expeditione christianorum militum orationibus ad Deum factis, imbres in siti illa impetravit. Quando non geniculationibus et jejunationibus nostris etiam siccitates sunt depulsae? Tunc et populus acclamans Deo deorum, qui solus potens, in Jovis nomine Deo nostro testimonium reddidit. Praeter haec depositum non abnegamus, matrimonium nullius adulteramus, pupillos pie tractamus, indigentibus refrigeramus, nulli malum pro malo reddimus. Viderint, qui sectam mentiuntur, quos et ipsi recusamus. Quis denique de nobis alio nomine queritur? quod aliud negotium patitur christianus, nisi suae sectae? quam incestam, quam crudelem, tanto tempore nemo probavit. Pro tanta innocentia, pro tanta probitate, pro justitia, pro pudicitia, pro fide, pro veritate, pro Deo vivo, cremamur; quod nec sacrilegi, nec hostes publici, verum nec tot majestatis rei pati solent. Nam et nunc a praeside legionis, et a praeside Mauritaniae vexatur hoc nomen, sed gladio tenus, sicut et a primordio mandatum est animadverti in hujusmodi. Sed majora certamina, majora sequuntur praemia.
pass_a_gloss: We do not frighten you, who do not fear: but I wish that we may be able to make all safe, by warning not to fight against God. You are able to perform the duty of your jurisdiction, and to remember humanity, or because you also are under the sword. For what else is commanded to you, than to condemn the guilty who have confessed, but to recall those who deny to torments? You see therefore how you yourselves act against the commands, so that you force those who have confessed to deny. So much do you confess that we are innocent, whom you do not wish to condemn immediately from the confession. But if you contend to destroy us, then you attack our innocence. How many presidents, and more constant and more cruel, have dissimulated in cases of this kind! Such as Cincius Severus, who himself gave a remedy to the Thystrians, how Christians might respond, so that they might be dismissed; Such as Vespronius Candidus, who dismissed a Christian, as if tumultuous, to satisfy his citizens; Such as Asper, who moderately harassed a man, and immediately released him, and did not compel him to make a sacrifice, having previously declared among the advocates and assessors, that he was grieved to have fallen into this case. Pudens also dismissed a Christian sent to him, having understood the shaking of his speech, with the same speech broken, without an accuser denying that he would hear the man according to the command. All these things can be suggested to you, both from duty, and from the same advocates, who themselves have benefits from Christians, although they shout what they want. For even a certain notary, when he was being thrown down by a demon, was freed: and a relative and a little boy of some, and how many honest men (for we do not speak of the common people) either from demons or from illnesses have been remedied! Even Severus, the father of Antoninus, was mindful of Christians. For he also sought out a Christian, Proculus, who was surnamed Torpacion, a procurator of Euhodea, who had once cured him with oil, and had him in his palace until his death: whom also Antoninus knew very well, having been educated on Christian milk. But even the most illustrious women and the most illustrious men, Severus, knowing them to be of this sect, not only did not harm, but also honored with testimony, and openly resisted the raging people against us. Also Marcus Aurelius, in the German expedition, having obtained rains from the prayers of Christian soldiers made to God, in that drought. When have our kneelings and fastings not even driven away droughts? Then also the people, shouting to the God of gods, who alone is powerful, in the name of Jupiter, gave testimony to our God. Besides these things, we do not deny a deposit, we do not adulterate anyone's marriage, we treat orphans piously, we refresh the needy, we return no evil for evil to anyone. Let those see, who lie about our sect, whom we also reject. Who finally complains about us with another name? What other business does a Christian suffer, except that of his own sect? Which, so incestuous, so cruel, no one has proven for so long a time. For such great innocence, for such great integrity, for justice, for chastity, for faith, for truth, for the living God, we are burned; which not even sacrilegious people, nor public enemies, but not even those who have committed so many crimes against majesty, usually suffer. For even now the name is harassed by the president of the legion, and by the president of Mauritania, but only with the sword, as it has been commanded from the beginning to take notice of such things. But greater struggles, greater rewards follow.
pass_b_english: We aren't trying to frighten you; you don't scare anyway. My aim is to keep everyone safe by warning you not to fight against God. You can do your job as governor and still remember basic humanity — especially since you, too, live under the sword. What exactly does your commission order? To condemn confessed criminals, and to send those who deny the charge to the rack. So look at what you're doing: you force the very people who have confessed to recant, which means you're acting against your own orders. You all but admit we're innocent when you refuse to condemn us on the spot after a confession. And if you press on to destroy us, you're not punishing guilt — you're attacking innocence.

Plenty of governors — tougher and more brutal than you — have quietly let this kind of case drop. Cincius Severus coached the Thystrians on how Christians would answer so he could release them. Vespronius Candidus dismissed a Christian as a mere disturber of the peace to calm his own citizens. Asper roughed a man up lightly, then let him go without demanding a sacrifice, after telling his legal advisers and assessors he regretted ever getting mixed up in the case. Pudens sent a Christian away after realizing his statement was incoherent; with the speech falling apart and no accuser present, he refused to hear the man, citing his orders. All this can be cited to you as a matter of duty — and your own legal advisers know it, since they've benefited from Christians themselves, no matter what they shout in court.

Even a notary, thrown down by a demon, was set free. Relatives and little children of prominent men — not to mention the men themselves, honest and high-ranking, not commoners — have been healed of demons or sickness. The emperor Severus, Antoninus' father, kept Christians in mind. He tracked down Proculus, surnamed Torpacion, procurator of Euhodea, who had once cured him with oil, and kept him in his palace until the man died; Antoninus knew him well, having been raised on a Christian woman's milk. Severus also knew that the most distinguished women and men belonged to this sect — and he not only refused to harm them, he honored them publicly and stood up to a mob raging against us. Marcus Aurelius, on campaign in Germany, got rain for his parched army through the prayers of Christian soldiers. When have our kneeling and fasting ever failed to break a drought? The crowd itself shouted to the God of gods, the only Power, invoking Jupiter's name while bearing witness to our God.

On top of that: we don't embezzle deposits, we don't violate anyone's marriage, we raise orphans with care, we relieve the poor, we return no evil for evil. Let the people who slander our sect look at the lives they themselves reject. Who accuses us under any other name? What crime does a Christian commit except belonging to this sect? And for all this time, no one has proved it incestuous or cruel. For such innocence, such integrity, for justice, chastity, faith, truth, and the living God — we are burned alive. Not even sacrilegious criminals, not even public enemies, not even those guilty of the worst treason, usually suffer this. Even now the name is harassed by the legion's commander and the governor of Mauretania — but only with the sword, as ordered from the start. Greater struggles lie ahead; greater rewards follow.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Latin text. Pass A is a faithful literal translation, and Pass B is a fluent rendering that preserves all semantic content, including the specific historical examples and the theological distinctions. The translation of 'lacte christiano' as 'Christian milk' (Pass A) and 'a Christian woman's milk' (Pass B) is a valid interpretive choice for the Latin, and the translation of 'scisso eodem elogio' is handled consistently. All clauses, including the list of virtues and the historical precedents, are present in both versions.
